subject: Pilot packaging and downgrade guarantees
messages:
From: Alyssa Romero <alyssa.romero@tumbleweed.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@tumbleweed.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot packaging and downgrade guarantees

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. We're narrowing down whether to run a 90-day pilot on Redwood, but we need clarity on packaging and downgrade rules before we commit. A few pragmatic questions: 

- For a pilot of our size (~120k tokens/day avg, spiking to 400k/day) do you recommend Compact (cost-first) or Throughput (dedicated) pilot?
- If we start in Compact and find latency/throughput limits, what's the upgrade path mid-pilot? Any proration or guaranteed credit if we upgrade?
- Conversely, if we start on Throughput and don't need it after 90 days, what's the downgrade/credit policy?
- Do you offer one-time pilot discounts or committed-credit pricing for pilots?
- We need an SLA uplift for pilot customers evaluating production readiness — is that possible for 90 days?

I've attached our usage snapshot for the last 30 days (tumbleweed-usage-summary.csv). Procurement may loop in some questions about PO timing and DocuSign.

Appreciate a concise recommendation so we can get internal sign-off.

Thanks,
Alyssa Romero
Head of ML Ops
Tumbleweed AI

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Romero <alyssa.romero@tumbleweed.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging and downgrade guarantees

Hi Alyssa — great question and thanks for the usage file. High level recommendation: start the pilot on Compact with an optional burst-throughput add-on. Rationale: Compact gives the best unit economics while your average token volume fits comfortably; burst add-on buys headroom for spikes without committing to a dedicated pool.

Quick answers:
- Compact vs Throughput: Compact + burst add-on recommended for pilots of this profile. If sustained 95th percentile throughput > 1.5M tokens/hour for more than two weeks, we should talk Dedicated (Throughput).
- Upgrade path: You can upgrade mid-pilot to a Dedicated pool. Upgrades are pro-rated for remaining days; we also offer a one-time credit equal to unused Compact committed capacity when we agree to a Dedicated reserved commit (limited to pilot-to-paid conversions).
- Downgrade policy: Downgrades from Dedicated back to Compact are allowed at the next billing cycle; no retroactive refunds but we'll provide a one-time service credit for the first 30 days if the Dedicated proved unnecessary and you were mis-sized based on our performance analysis.
- Pilot discounts: We can approve a one-time pilot discount for evaluation customers — discount percentage is governed by deal size and conversion commitment.
- SLA uplift: We can provide a limited SLA uplift for 90-day pilots under an exception — requires sign-off from revenue ops.

I've attached a short proposal (Tumbleweed-pilot-proposal-v1.pdf) with pricing bands, suggested metrics to track, and an outline of the upgrade/downgrade mechanics. If this direction works, I can pull finance and prod-ops into the thread to finalize discount/SLA terms and get a DocuSign ready.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Tumbleweed-pilot-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: Alyssa Romero <alyssa.romero@tumbleweed.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@tumbleweed.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging and downgrade guarantees

Thanks Markus — that helps. Two follow-ups from procurement/execs: 

1) Can you confirm the max discount you might offer for a 90-day pilot for a company of our size if we commit to a purchase order and a 12-month conversion window?
2) We need the SLA uplift (99.9% availability target, escalation path and response times) documented in writing — is that part of the pilot exception?

Procurement also asked whether a DocuSign + PO workflow can be started this week so finance can pre-approve.

If you prefer, we can jump on a 20–30 minute call to finalize.

—Alyssa

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot packaging and downgrade guarantees — approval request (TW-2028-113)

Ben / Lauren,

Forwarding Alyssa's asks (excerpt below) — they want a firm discount for a 90-day pilot plus a documented SLA uplift (99.9% target) and a DocuSign/PO flow. Deal details: projected pilot consumption ~120k tokens/day avg, spikes to 400k; if all goes well they'd convert within 12 months and likely commit to a mid-sized reserved capacity.

Excerpt from Alyssa: 
> "Can you confirm the max discount you might offer for a 90-day pilot for a company of our size if we commit to a purchase order and a 12-month conversion window?"

What I'm proposing: authorize a one-time pilot discount up to 20% on the Compact pilot fee, plus an SLA exception for 90 days (on the condition we log agreed SLOs and an escalation path). In exchange we ask for a conversion intent (non-binding letter) and a HubSpot deal conversion flag to route to AMs. If 20% is too aggressive, approve a 15% cap and I'll negotiate down with Alyssa.

Also calling out that we should offer the burst-throughput add-on as a paid optional line item rather than defaulting them into Dedicated. That reduces our risk for mistaken dedicated sizing.

Can you confirm approval and any guardrails (limits, necessary revenue ops sign-off) so I can respond to procurement?

Thanks,
Markus

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot packaging and downgrade guarantees — approval request (TW-2028-113)

Markus / Ben —

Approve but with conditions:

- Max pilot discount: 15% (one-time). We can go to 20% only if legal and revenue ops approve an explicit conversion milestone (e.g., commit to a reserved monthly commit if usage >= X for 30 days).
- SLA uplift: approve 90-day SLA exception (99.9% availability) provided the customer signs a trial SLA addendum and we limit escalations to our standard enterprise on-call (no on-prem hands-on). I want the trial-SLA addendum attached to the DocuSign packet.
- Attachments & billing: require PO + DocuSign. Finance needs HubSpot deal ID (TW-2028-113) populated before DocuSign begins.

Also suggest offering a bundled "Quantization & Cache" feature pack at a small add-on price (helps reduce token cost and gives them an optimization path post-pilot). Mention the pack in the proposal but keep it optional.

If that works I authorize Markus to finalize the offer and send to Alyssa.

-Lauren
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Romero <alyssa.romero@tumbleweed.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging and downgrade guarantees

Hi Alyssa — quick update and next steps. Thank you for the details — we've reviewed and can commit to the following pilot package: 

- Pilot plan: Compact pilot with optional burst-throughput add-on (you can enable bursts programmatically).
- Approved one-time pilot discount: 15% off Compact pricing for the 90-day pilot (conditional per Lauren's note).
- SLA uplift: 90-day trial SLA at 99.9% availability via a trial-SLA addendum (attached). Escalation and response times follow our enterprise on-call process.
- Upgrade path: mid-pilot upgrade to Dedicated is allowed and pro-rated; if we mis-size Dedicated we'll provide a one-time service credit covering the first 30 days post-upgrade as described in the proposal.
- Optional add-on: "Quantization & Cache" optimization pack (recommended) — listed as an optional line item in the attached proposal.

Next steps for you:
1) Confirm you accept the 15% pilot discount and SLA addendum.
2) Procurement: please populate the HubSpot deal (TW-2028-113) and send the PO to procurement@redwood.ai; once PO is uploaded we'll trigger the DocuSign packet.
3) I'll attach the finalized proposal and trial-SLA addendum to DocuSign once procurement indicates they're ready.

Attachments: Tumbleweed-pilot-proposal-v1.pdf; pilot-sla-exception-request.docx
DocuSign link (will be active once PO is received): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/TW-PILOT-2028

If you'd like a 20-30 minute call to walk the team through the upgrade mechanics and the quantization pack, I'm happy to set that up.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
